STATIC

A mystery detective horror set in a remote Alaskan town, where an unseen force reaches through the television signal, abducting people without a trace. As reality begins to unravel, you must investigate the disappearances, uncover the truth behind the enigmatic Gray Signal, and decide the fate of a town haunted by its past.

01 — Game concept & plot

Genre, Gameplay Mechanics, and Story

STATIC is a third-person mystery-horror adventure that blends investigation, survival, and action into a narrative-driven experience where every major decision carries lasting consequences.

Genre
Mystery-horror adventure
Perspective
Third-person
Players
Single-player
For fans of
Alan Wake · Heavy Rain · The Vanishing of Ethan Carter

Story

STATIC is built upon the events of the novel Myst, but instead of retelling its story, it invites players to rewrite it. The game follows the same world, characters, and central mystery while allowing pivotal choices to reshape the narrative and the destiny of the heroes.


In 2018, Saoirse Barrell returns to the Alaskan town Mag Point: the place she swore never to see again. Ten years earlier, her ten-year-old brother, Caleb, vanished without a trace alongside four other children. The town never found answers, and neither did she. Ironically, she comes back for something utterly mundane: to retrieve her old medical records. The moment she arrives, people begin disappearing again. When Saoirse's father becomes the prime suspect, she is forced to launch her own investigation.


She finds ally in Ian Demme, her former high school boyfriend. Ten years ago, she left Mag Point without saying goodbye, shattering his life and leaving wounds that never truly healed. Their unexpected reunion forces them to confront both their shared past and the secrets they have kept from one another.


As the mysterious Gray Signal spreads through the town again, Ian and Saoirse must uncover the truth behind the disappearances that have haunted the town for decades. But in STATIC, the truth is never fixed. Every crucial decision has the power to alter relationships, reshape the investigation, and change the fate of their loved ones.

Two protagonists, one town

Players explore the isolated Alaskan town of Mag Point, uncovering clues behind a series of mysterious disappearances while confronting hostile entities emerging from the enigmatic Gray Signal. The story is experienced through two playable protagonists, Ian and Saoirse, whose gameplay styles complement one another.

Ian Demme

Action · Close quarters · Investigation

A young local troublemaker, anchors the game's tense, investigation line, close-quarters encounters, relying on firearms and hand-to-hand combat when the threat gets physical.

Saoirse Barrell

Stealth · Observation · Narrative

Reluctantly returned after years in New York City, approaches danger through stealth, observation, and careful infiltration, offering a contrasting perspective on both the narrative and gameplay.

Gameplay

The core gameplay is built around five interconnected pillars.

Investigation20%

Collecting evidence and reconstructing events on a detective board to identify suspects, motives, and hidden connections.

Narrative25%

Branching dialogue, cinematic sequences, and character relationships that shape both the immediate story and the ending.

Exploration25%

Searching locations, environmental storytelling, hidden documents, and optional discoveries.

Combat15%

Firearm and hand-to-hand encounters centered primarily around Ian's gameplay.

Stealth15%

Infiltration, evasion, and silent navigation, primarily experienced through Saoirse.

A living world

The world itself is dynamic. Locations can be explored during both day and night, and the transition between them fundamentally changes the experience. Areas that are safe during daylight may become hostile after dark, introducing new enemies and altered routes, that question the very nature of reality. You can never be certain how much of what you're experiencing is real. Players will encounter environmental changes, and previously inaccessible opportunities. Players are encouraged to revisit familiar locations under different conditions, as the town itself evolves alongside the story.

Innovative mechanics

Two systems set STATIC apart from a traditional detective horror.

The Gray Signal

A mysterious phenomenon that obscures hostile entities from normal perception. During both combat and stealth encounters, players must actively operate a retransmission device to intercept the Gray Signal, revealing enemies that would otherwise remain invisible. Maintaining the signal becomes a constant tactical consideration, transforming every encounter into a balance between awareness, survival, and resource management.

The investigation board

Unlike conventional detective games, the investigation board provides no guidance, hints, or hidden validation. Players independently connect evidence and formulate conclusions, making genuine deductions instead of following predetermined solutions. Three pivotal investigation decisions serve as major narrative turning points. An incorrect conclusion does not result in failure or a game over. Instead, the story branches in a different direction.

Your Conclusion Has Altered The Story

03 — Interactive dialogue

Interactive dialogue

A branching dialogue scene that shapes the course of the story. Two main playable characters, Ian and Saoirse cross paths by chance in Mag Point for the first time since 2008, when Saoirse left for New York City without a word, abandoning both the town and the relationship they once shared. Their unexpected reunion comes just as people begin disappearing again, pulling them back into a mystery they thought had been left behind.
